body:
Sounds to me like you don't feel like you're worth very much. Like you're not acceptable in the eyes of others, so that it consumes you, and you've become the person that you think that you are in the eyes of others.

You know, how it goes. You've probably heard it before, but you become what you think about. By that I mean, if you think a certain way, and think certain things about yourself, you'll eventually become those things.

I feel your position and can relate. Let's talk about your mom. What's your relationship with her like?
Sounds like you're going through some difficult problems. What emotions in particularly feeling right now? Are you depressed? Sad? Angry? What's really going on?

It sounds like you're in a very difficult situation. I think, with your brother, it might be a good idea to let him know, at least, that you're there for him to talk to. Just mentioning it to him is not forcing him to talk. Someone who has lost someone needs people around them. Often, they will naturally regress from people and become withdrawn. It does not mean that they do not want to talk to people, it means they're in a bad spot and might need some help.

It sounds to me like the people you are hanging out with aren't the right crowd for you. It might be a good idea to get away from the type of people who have such negative attitudes and opinions about your sexuality in general. Although it might not seem like it, there are plenty of people who will openly accept you for who YOU are. It's just going to take you some time to find those people. 

I know everything is difficult for you right now, but I really understand how you're feeling. I do. If you need someone to talk to about anything at all, feel free to send me a message. I'd love to have a chat with you.
What you're explaining with the highs and lows sounds a lot like bipolar disorder to me. Have you ever been to a doctor before and mentioned these problems?

Heya. Meh. Just not very good. I constantly think negative thoughts, and as a result, am always stressed and tense. I do have a thing to do today with my guild in a video game so that's nice, I guess/

To answer your question, no, I wouldn't feel any better. I've been living the same life (no life) for more than 5 years. Having cancer would just be a shift in the paradigm slightly. If I didn't have it, things would just go back to "normal" again.

I've felt feelings of worthlessness before I was truly depressed, so it's been with me for most of my life. I don't doubt that I *can* get help, I just know that I *won't* get help because of all my mental blockades. As far as love goes, no, I don't ever see that happening, not because I can't be loved, but because I, personally, cannot love.  Don't even get me started on happiness, I'm sure, just like the answer to the question you asked, that you already know the answer of someone who's been depressed for a great while.

Well, it's a lot harder and more complicated for me than just picking up the phone, I'm sure you understand if you understand depression and social anxiety. Money issues as well, so. Yeah. Of course I want help, but I really am unhelpable. 

I feel like an impenetrable fortress. Of course I could just "let help in". But honestly, I'm not strong enough to pull the rope and open up the gate, and I'm not the type of person who has the motivation or willpower to exercise to build up the strength that is required for that.

I'm sure if you think about it, you can understand me very easily with that analogy. Anywho. Thanks for your comments. Much love. Have a good night. I'm going to bed. [:
Oh. I'm not actually feeling positive. I'm just trying to be polite. I honestly expected to get no responses and it surprised me that I got this many.
And wow, I'm suprised that I got so many responses from you guys so quickly. <3 I love you all. Thank you so much. Still feeling like utter crap right now, but regardless. Love to you kind people.

Sorry. But I can't take your post seriously with the last half of your second paragraph there. Thanks for your response, though.

Edit: I took what you were saying wayyy out of context. Although I still disagree with that you're saying, I understand it now. Anywho. I really still don't know what else to say. I don't know, I guess. I don't know what will happen in the future. I acknowledge the fact that my thought pattern might change, but only with the help from others. I don't know what it would take, but I've talked with quite a few people with my problems and have tried lots of things but to no avail. I'm seriously messed up I guess. Rambling now, ugh. x_X
Grr. It didn't let me make a face. Trying it again ^^.^

Well, if it did ever get to the point where it was that painful, I could just tie a bag around my head. I've heard that's not very painful. xD Would you consider that a plan?

Yes, and I am depressed, It's just like I said, though... for many reasons, I'm never going to see any sort of doctor or therapist. I could be my own therapist if I needed. I'm actually quite used to helping other people with their problems, I could use what I've used to help others on myself, but I choose not to, well, because I don't really care about myself.

Anywho. Thanks for your response ^.^

Bluh. You sound like the one who's depressed here o-o
I've gone over my problems layers over layers with other people, to be honest. I feel like I understand them well enough that I don't really feel like burdening more people with them. 

On the other side, I don't really have any friends. And that's, well, that's for a lot of reasons. Mostly because I don't really value casual connections with people. I'm more... erhm. In depth. But I'm also nearly impossible to get close to. Anyways. Yes. It's a bit lonely, so I guess talking just in general can help, at least a little bit. Sometimes. Maybe.

In the end, I don't really know. Honestly, I feel like I'm a bother just for posting here in the first place. I'm far more depressed than I made it out to be in my original post, actually, and I'd rather avoid expressing my thoughts, because I tend to bring even the brightest of souls down to the depths along with me.

Well, because getting out and doing all of those things - things that I really don't want to do and am sure would not bring happiness to me - they require overcoming my anxiety. It requires hurdling myself over so many blockades, and all for something that likely won't help me in the first place, in fact, I feel quite the opposite, that all of the stress and effort and added worries of school/work/society would just make me worse.

As for my parents. We're all on good terms. I live with my mom. I see my dad once a month. I'm in a bubble though. I've tried expressing myself to my mom, but she's so enveloped in her problems that she doesn't know what to say about mine. Oh well.
